Turbine is a network dynamics simulation tool that can model the propagation and dissipation of perturbations in complex networks.
The 'communicating vessels' model used in Turbine assumes that every affected node dissipates an equal amount of energy in each time step, resulting in exponential decay of perturbations.
Networks with pronounced modular structure (5% inter-modular edges) trap and dissipate perturbations much slower than networks with fuzzy modular structure (40% inter-modular edges).
Perturbation centrality is defined as the reciprocal of the 'silencing time' - the time needed to dissipate a perturbation of 10*n units (where n is the number of nodes) below a threshold of 1 unit.
Perturbation centrality correlates with closeness, community, and weighted degree centralities, but captures both local and global properties of nodes in information propagation.
In networks with pronounced modular structure, inter-modular non-hub nodes had higher perturbation centrality than intra-modular hubs.
In real-world networks which tend to have fuzzy modular structure, intra-modular hubs were 87% more efficient at dissipating perturbations than inter-modular non-hubs.
In the Met-tRNA synthetase protein structure network, perturbation centrality correctly identified the active site and tRNA binding sites as key regions for propagating perturbations.

In the yeast interactome, changes in perturbation centrality under different stress conditions recapitulated known functional changes, such as the down-regulation of ribosome synthesis and protein translation.
The average perturbation centrality of the heat-shocked yeast interactome was 40.5% lower than the unstressed interactome, indicating reduced perturbation propagation.
Only 42 of the 100 nodes with highest perturbation centrality in the unstressed yeast interactome were also in the top 100 under heat shock, while 65-68 overlapped under oxidative and osmotic stress.
Turbine can handle multiple, repeated or continuous perturbations introduced at any time-steps, and can also change the network structure during simulations.
Turbine enables the analysis of large networks (millions of nodes and edges) on a standard desktop computer.
The Turbine software and the perturbation centrality measure may provide novel options to assess signaling, drug action, environmental and social interventions.
The novelty and usefulness of perturbation centrality was validated in several model, biological and social networks.
